parts.article:
Mammoth Kill
 
What Led to the disappearance of the giant mammals? Kate Wong examines the theories
 
(A) Although it's hard to imagine in this age of urban sprawl and automobiles, North America once belonged to huge, elephant-like mammoths, camels, bear-sized beavers and other giant beasts, collectively known as 'megafauna'. Some 11,000 years ago, however, these large-bodied mammals—about 70 species in all—disappeared. Their demise coincided roughly with the arrival of humans on the continent and dramatic climate change—factors that have inspired several theories about the die-off. Yet despite decades of scientific investigation, the exact cause remains a mystery. Now new findings offer support to one of these controversial hypotheses: that human hunting drove these huge megafauna species to extinction.
 
(B) This belief resulted in the overkill model which emerged in the 1960s, when it was put forth by Paul S. Martin of the University of Arizona. Since then, critics have charged that no archaeological remains exist to support the idea that the first Americans hunted to the extent necessary to cause these extinctions, but at the annual meeting of the Society of Vertebrate Paleontology in Mexico City in October 1999, specialist John Alroy of the University of California at Santa Barbara argued that, in fact, hunting-driven extinction is not only plausible, it was unavoidable. He has determined, using a computer simulation, that even a very modest amount of hunting would have wiped out these animals. Assuming an initial human population of 100 people that grew no more than two per cent annually, Alroy determined that, if each band of, say, 50 people killed 15 to 20 large animals a year, humans could have eliminated the animal populations within 1,000 years. Large mammals in particular would have been vulnerable to the pressure because they have longer gestation periods than smaller mammals and their young require extended care.
 
(C) However, not everyone agrees with Alroy's assessment. For one thing, the results depend on population-size estimates for the extinct animals—estimates that are not necessarily reliable. But a more specific criticism comes from mammal expert Ross D. E. MacPhee of the American Museum of Natural History in New York City, who points out that the relevant archaeological record contains barely a dozen examples of stone points embedded in mammoth bones (and none, it should be noted, are known from other megafaunal remains)—hardly what one might expect if hunting drove these animals to extinction. Furthermore, some of these species had a vast range, covering the whole continent—the Jefferson's ground sloth, for example, lived as far north as the Yukon and as far south as Mexico—which would have made hunting them in numbers sufficient to cause their extinction rather unlikely, he says.
 
(D) MacPhee agrees that humans most likely brought about these extinctions (as well as others around the world that coincided with human arrival), but not directly. Rather than through hunting, he suggests that people may have introduced a deadly disease, perhaps through their dogs or accompanying vermin, which then spread wildly among the native species because of their low resistance to the new introductions. Repeated outbreaks of a deadly disease could thus quickly drive them to the point of no return. So far, MacPhee does not have empirical evidence for this theory, and it will not be easy to come by: such disease would kill far too quickly to leave its signature on the bones themselves. But he hopes that analyses of tissue and DNA from the most recent animal remains will eventually reveal the microbes responsible.
 
(E) The third explanation for what brought on this North American extinction does not involve human beings. Instead, its proponents blame the loss on the climate. The Pleistocene epoch in question witnessed considerable climate instability, explains Russell W. Graham of the Denver Museum of Nature and Science. As a result, their regular habitats disappeared, and species that had once formed communities split apart. For some animals, this brought opportunity. For much of the megafauna, however, the increasingly uniform terrain left them with shrinking geographical ranges—a death sentence for large animals, which need correspondingly large ranges. Although these creatures managed to maintain viable populations through most of the Pleistocene period, the final major climate fluctuation pushed them over the edge, Graham says.
 
(F) For his part, Alroy is still convinced that human hunters were the destroyers of the giant animals. The overkill model explains everything the disease and climate scenarios explain, he asserts, and in addition makes accurate predictions about which species would eventually become extinct.

groups.contentHtml:
Three theories have been put forward to explain the disappearance of the different species of large mammals that inhabited 11,000 years ago. The , proposed around fifty years ago by Paul S. Martin, blames by people for mass extinction. Computer calculations seem to support this explanation, but critics question the reliability of the figures they are based on.
The second theory suggests that humans introduced a which wiped out the large mammals. However, so far this theory also lacks any .
The final theory suggests that this period experienced significant , which eventually led to the loss of habitat and to the division of the that some of the large mammals had organized.

analyses.content: “Inhabited” 对应原文的 “belonged to / lived in” 语境。
(Paragraph A) “Although it's hard to imagine..., North America once belonged to huge, elephant-like mammoths...”
题目说大型哺乳动物11,000年前栖息在____。原文A段第一句提到“North America once belonged to huge... mammals”，第二句提到“Some 11,000 years ago... disappeared”，填 North America。
题目说大约50年前由Paul S. Martin提出的____。原文B段第一句提到“This belief resulted in the overkill model which emerged in the 1960s, when it was put forth by Paul S. Martin”，填 overkill model。
“Proposed... by” 对应 “put forth by”。
(Paragraph B) “This belief resulted in the overkill model which emerged in the 1960s...”
题目说该模型将大规模灭绝归咎于人类的____。原文A段末尾和B段都提到核心观点是“human hunting drove these... to extinction”，填 hunting。
题目已有 “by people”，因此只需填 “hunting”，不要填 “human hunting” 造成语义重复。
(Paragraph A) “...that human hunting drove these huge megafauna species to extinction.”
“Introduced a...” 对应原文的 “introduced a...”。
题目说第二种理论认为人类引入了一种____。原文D段提到MacPhee建议人们可能引入了一种“deadly disease（致命疾病）”，填 deadly disease。
(Paragraph D) “...suggests that people may have introduced a deadly disease...”
题目说目前该理论缺乏任何____。原文D段提到“So far, MacPhee does not have empirical evidence for this theory（目前MacPhee没有此理论的实证证据）”，填 empirical evidence。
“Lacks any” 对应 “does not have”。
(Paragraph D) “So far, MacPhee does not have empirical evidence for this theory...”
题目说最后的理论认为这一时期经历了显著的____。原文E段提到该时期见证了相当大的“climate instability（气候不稳定）”，填 climate instability。
“Experienced significant” 对应 “witnessed considerable”。
(Paragraph E) “The Pleistocene epoch in question witnessed considerable climate instability...”
(Paragraph E) “...and species that had once formed communities split apart.”
“Division of” 对应 “split apart”，“organized” 对应 “formed”。
题目说最终导致了栖息地的丧失和大型哺乳动物组织的____的分裂。原文E段提到“species that had once formed communities split apart（曾经形成群落/社区的物种分裂了）”，填 communities。

groups.description:
Complete the summary below.
Choose NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from the passage for each answer.
Write your answers in boxes 14–20 on your answer sheet.

groups.contentHtml:
21
Too little evidence exists to support the hunting theory.
22
The bigger the animal, the bigger the territory it requires for survival.
23
Globally, humans have been indirectly responsible for the elimination of many species.
24
Population estimates can be used to understand how large mammals became extinct.
25
Scientific examination of fossil remains may provide some proof for one of the theories.
26
Environmental changes negatively affected the social groupings of some large species.

questions.question: Too little evidence exists to support the hunting theory.

analyses.content: 题目说支持狩猎理论的证据太少。原文C段 MacPhee 指出考古记录中“barely a dozen examples（仅有十几例）”石镞嵌在骨头里，这“hardly what one might expect（很难符合人们的预期）”，即证据不足，选 B。
“Too little evidence” 对应 “barely a dozen examples / hardly what one might expect”。
(Paragraph C) “...criticism comes from... MacPhee... barely a dozen examples... hardly what one might expect...”

questions.question: The bigger the animal, the bigger the territory it requires for survival.

analyses.content: 题目说动物越大，生存所需的领地越大。原文E段 Graham 解释说气候变化对大型动物是死刑判决，因为它们“need correspondingly large ranges（需要相应大的范围）”，选 C。
“Bigger... territory” 对应 “large animals... large ranges”。
(Paragraph E) “...a death sentence for large animals, which need correspondingly large ranges... Graham says.”

questions.question: Globally, humans have been indirectly responsible for the elimination of many species.

analyses.content: (Paragraph D) “MacPhee agrees that humans most likely brought about these extinctions... but not directly.”
题目说在全球范围内，人类**间接（indirectly）**对许多物种的灭绝负责。原文D段 MacPhee 同意人类导致了灭绝（brought about these extinctions），但“not directly（不是直接的）”，而是通过引入疾病，选 B。
“Indirectly responsible” 对应 “humans most likely brought about... but not directly”。

questions.question: Population estimates can be used to understand how large mammals became extinct.

analyses.content: 题目说人口估计可用于理解大型哺乳动物如何灭绝。原文B段 Alroy 使用计算机模拟，假设了“initial human population（初始人口）”和增长率来推断灭绝是不可避免的，选 A。
“Population estimates” 对应 “Assuming an initial human population... determined that...”。
(Paragraph B) “John Alroy... determined... Assuming an initial human population of 100...”

questions.question: Scientific examination of fossil remains may provide some proof for one of the theories.

analyses.content: 题目说对化石遗骸的科学检查可能为其中一个理论提供证据。原文D段 MacPhee 希望通过对最近动物遗骸的“analyses of tissue and DNA（组织和DNA分析）”能揭示致病微生物，选 B。
“Scientific examination of fossil” 对应 “analyses of tissue and DNA from... animal remains”。
(Paragraph D) “But he [MacPhee] hopes that analyses of tissue and DNA...”

questions.question: Environmental changes negatively affected the social groupings of some large species.

analyses.content: 题目说环境变化负面影响了一些大型物种的社会群体（social groupings）。原文E段 Graham 指出由于气候不稳定，曾经形成“communities（群落/社区）”的物种分裂了（split apart），选 C。
“Social groupings” 对应 “communities”，“Negatively affected” 对应 “split apart / disappeared”。
(Paragraph E) “...species that had once formed communities split apart... Graham explains.”
